utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [B/C/S on English channel]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, on this Monday, the 12th of February, 2007, we're continuing our proceedings and we're going to have three witnesses which are scheduled for the week. I'd like to welcome all those in the courtroom, the Prosecution, the ladies and gentlemen of the Defence counsel, and the accused. There seems to be a problem. Mr. Praljak doesn't seem to be hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not receiving interpretation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently the accused aren't receiving the interpretation. Yes they are. Everything is all right now. Things are working. Good. Now, the interpreters with asked for the following: They say that they are having great difficulty following us and that this makes it difficult for them to translate when it is very fast. So I would like to ask one and all to speak more slowly so that our interpreters can follow and do their job. That's what I wanted to say. Having done that, I'm going to give the floor to Madam Registrar for two IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, two documents have been submitted. There's a list by 5D to be tendered through Witness Patrick Van Der Weijden. That will be given number IC 387. And a list by OTP which is an objection to documents tendered by 5D through Witness -- sorry, by 3D through Witness Enes Vukotic, and that one will be given IC 388. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Last week we had to adjourn very quickly because of the problems related to the snow. As you know, our expert witness will be back in due course for the cross-examination. I think he'll be back fairly quickly, which will allow us to go ahead with everything in our heads. We'll remember what was going on. Now, as far as the witnesses that are going to address the question of sniping are concerned, today we have three scheduled, and having studied the timetable, the Prosecution has asked for 30 minutes for the next one. I hope they'll be able to get through it even quicker. And as we see that the same questions are being asked again and again, cropping up again, we feel that 45 minutes will be sufficient for the Defence teams to conduct their cross-examination. So I would like to appeal to the Prosecution to try and get through the summary in 20 minutes, or 20 minutes per each witness, to allow 45 minutes to the Defence teams, which means double the time to cross-examine. Having said that, may we have the first witness shown into the courtroom. Mr. Usher, would you go and fetch the witness. Good afternoon, Mr. Bos. I see that we have six documents for the next witness, Dzemal Barakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours; good afternoon everyone in the courtroom. Yes, Your Honours, there's six items on the exhibit list but, you know, those items include the 360 photograph and the video, and, in fact, as far as documents are concerned, I think I will only have two documents to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I'd like to check that you can hear the interpretation of what I'm saying. If you understand tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we're going to have you take the solemn declaration, so would you please stand. But before that could you tell me your first name, last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dzemal Barakovic, the 7th of February, 1949.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm -- I do have one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which one, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a professional fireman in the fire unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would you now go ahead and read the solemn declaration that the usher's going to hand to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. You may be seated. Just some preliminary information from me. You're going to be answering questions put to you by the Prosecution first. You've already met the Prosecutor either yesterday or this morning, and that is the first stage. After that, the Defence counsel and the accused have 45 minutes to ask you their questions within the cross-examination, and possibly the four Judges sitting up at the Bench might ask you questions as well. If you have any problems, don't hesitate to let me know, especially if you have health problems. So don't hesitate to tell me straight away. Having said that, I give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Barakovic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Mr. Barakovic I'm first of all going to give a small summary of your statement and I'll read that out. The witness was a resident of West Mostar. On 30 June, 1993, he was arrested and imprisoned in Heliodrom. On 24 July, 1993, he was released and went back to his home. Around 17 August, 1993, he and his family were expelled to East Mostar by HVO soldiers. The witness joined the East Mostar fire brigade as a driver. He saw the victim Enver Dziho after he had been shot by a sniper. The witness was also present when Stojan Kacic was carrying Enver Dziho on a stretcher. Was shot by a sniper. That concludes my summary. Witness, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions first about a statement. Is it correct that you made a written statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 31st of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at the time you provided this written statement, did you answer the questions to the investigator truthfully?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you answer the questions freely, that is without any coercion?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at the conclusion of that interview, sir, was the statement read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you then sign the statement in the English language?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher now to provide the witness with the bundle of exhibits for Mr. Barakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Mr. Barakovic, I would like to ask you to turn to Exhibit number 9855 in this bundle, which is the first document in this bundle. And this would be an English version of your statement. And what I would like to ask you is whether you could confirm that the signature on the bottom of each page is, in fact, your signature.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that we met this morning, Witness Barakovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at that meeting, did I ask you whether you wanted to correct anything to your statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you have any corrections to make to your statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So at this stage I would like to tender the statement of Mr. Barakovic into evidence as Exhibit 9858.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that in 2004, in the summer of 2004, you met with an investigator and a photographer of the ICTY in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it true that at that time you were asked a series of questions relating to the sniping incident that is discussed in your statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And were these questions and answers actually videotaped? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honours, I'm going to show a video clip, and I would like to forewarn everyone here in the courtroom, the video clip, there's a sound problem in the video clip. The first part is okay, but the second part of the video clip does not have any sound. Nevertheless, I would like to show the whole video. And I suggest first to play the whole tape and then to play the tape again and then that second time I will stop the tape for a few moments and ask the witness a few questions. But if we can now play Exhibit 9140 clip of incident number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Barakovic, to the best of your recollection, could you please indicate where you saw the body of Enver Dziho lying. Lying." "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. To the best of your recollection could you please walk the path that two paramedics followed carrying the body of Enver Dziho on a stretcher, and could you stop at the spot where the paramedic, Stojan Kacic, was shot? "Witness: [Witness complies]"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of general questions and then we'll play the tape again and I'll ask you a few more specific questions. Let me first ask you, did you recognise yourself on this videotape?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you understand the instructions that were given to you, that were put to you by the investigator on that day?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just one thing. In one of the questions put to you by the investigator, the investigator was referring to Mr. Stojan -- Mr. Stojan Kacic as a paramedic. Was this Stojan Kacic actually a paramedic or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he was a paramedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, I would again ask the videotape to be played, and I will stop at a -- on --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Stop here. Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, where we stopped, you've been asked the question where you saw Enver Dziho lying in 1993, and you point with your arm. But can you explain to the Court where you are actually pointing to, because we see a fence here in front of the photograph. Is this -- is it actually in front of the fence where Enver Dziho was lying or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: The exit in front of the department store there's a road and there's a small building which was used as a woodshed and then steps leading to in front of the house, to in front of this shed. There was a garage up there too. That's where I found Enver Dziho lying down, and Ibro Spago, who went to help him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And this wooden fence that we see here on the picture, did that exist in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, because the Serb who owned the house, it was a Serb house, he returned and then put this fence up around his house and around his garden with this kind of wooden fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Barakovic, do you recall why we actually -- why the videotape wasn't taken at the stop where Enver Dziho was actually lying but over here? Do you recall why the video was taken here?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Because we weren't able to enter because it was fenced up. So we didn't have access. And as it's private property, we weren't able to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, did I ask you this morning to make a drawing of what -- what's behind, in fact, the wooden fence and where you actually saw the body of Enver Dziho? Did I ask you to make a drawing this morning?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like to show the following drawing that was made by the witness this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And, Witness, maybe -- maybe could you -- could you explain what you've been drawing here? Let's first just ask so that everyone knows where we are on the photograph. Where did you draw the fence that we've just seen on the video? And you will have to point at the photograph on the overhead so that everyone can see.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's it. That's where we filmed and where we were talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Who have you indicated under number 3?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was there when I made the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. So number 3 is your position when -- when you were there when the videotape was being recorded.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, can you then explain maybe -- what's under number 1 and number 2?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1 is Ibro Spago, who came to help Dziho, who was wounded. He's number 1. And number 2 is Dziho, who was wounded. He was lying down. Or both of them were actually lying down, because the sniper shot while they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you're talking about two persons who got one -- who got wounded, and you saw that they were lying there. Could you just again clarify the record. Who was number 1 and who was number 2? Could you give the full names of both persons.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to show you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, just --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just give me the name of who was number 1.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1 was Ibro Spago. He came to help Enver Dziho. Enver Dziho is number 2. He was the person who was wounded, and that's the spot where he was lying, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps with your permission I might be allowed to say that in view of this -- the fact that the sketch was drawn by the witness and when we look at the findings on page 31 with incident 11 with the expert witness, it's difficult to find one's way. So perhaps if the witness could be asked about incident 11 in the expert report and compare that to the witness's sketch to show us where the bullet came from, because I'm not sure things can be understood this way and we'll just lose time in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Mr. Kovacic. Mr. Bos, Mr. Kovacic has explained it all. What we're interested in is where the shot came from the witness. So perhaps you can ask the witness if he can make his contribution to clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as what the witness actually saw a person being shot, that's not Enver Dziho. The witness saw the body of Enver Dziho, but he didn't see Enver Dziho being shot. The person he was -- he did being shot was the person who was -- who has not been indicated here on this drawing. This is -- this is the place from where Enver Dziho's body was being carried to the next place where actually the witness saw somebody being shot, Mr. Stojan. So it's -- I don't really see the need. I don't see the objection that Mr. Kovacic is making. And what I -- what I would like the witness to do is maybe indicate on the drawing how the body of Enver Dziho was being carried and in which direction the body of Enver Dziho was being carried, and that's the purpose of this drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just a moment. Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we're going to have a problem because, according to the proofing chart provided to us by the Prosecutor, with all the incidents and the witnesses per incident, under incident 11, it says the Enver Dziho case and that's the one we're dealing with. So if the witness didn't see the victim fall casualty, then I don't think it's going to be much help to us. And now suddenly there's another incident that wasn't dealt with in the findings. The incident that was dealt with was Enver Dziho. So we all seem to be under a miscomprehension.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The incident that is concerned here is the incident of Mr. Stojan Kacic who has been shot and not -- as far as this witness is concerned, he can effective about where Mr. Stojan Kacic has been shot and not where Enver Dziho was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Petkovic Defence understood it was both. So can we be crystal clear. According to the documentation we had, it was both those victims that were included in this incident, and both are referred to in the expert witness's summary. So all I want to be is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, both persons were victims of a sniping shot but both the expert and this witness are only testifying about how Mr. Stojan Kacic was shot and from which direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. That's most helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that's the correct information. From the first sentence of the expert witness with incident 11 it says that he was a middle aged man, that the victim was a middle aged man crossing the street next to the Razvitak building, and then the next sentence was a description, to my mind, because there was no medical documentation, and it says that one of the people administering first aid - and now we seed see that he wasn't a paramedic either - was hit in the leg while attempting to assist victim B. And in this description, Enver Dziho is mentioned as a victim and Mr. Stojan Kacic is mentioned just by the by. So I'm not quite clear on that. What victim did the expert witness deal with when he wrote his report and description of incident 11? That's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And that's what I've been saying. It's Mr. Stojan Kacic, and in the expert report, that is victim Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I was taking it that when the Prosecution tell us, as Mr. Bos did a few minutes ago, unequivocally that it is only dealing with that one victim and that the expert is only dealing with that one victim, then whatever was in the expert report initially, that is the position for the rest of the case. And if I'm crystal clear about that, then I do understand Mr. Kovacic's difficulty, given that that's not what was said in the report. But if that's where we are now, there's this just this one victim and there's no doubt about that, then Defence won't be mislead and that's where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos, I have the expert report before me, and I'm -- I'm looking at incident 11 where it says on the 30th of October, 1993, victim P was shot while crossing a road near the Razvitak building, and then the expert adds: "One of the ambulance personnel," whether it was driver or a paramedic isn't clear, "victim Q was shot in the leg while trying to move victim P on a stretcher to the ambulance." So one could understand it that victim Q is the number 1 on the sketch, on the witness sketch, and the number 2 is victim P. One could take it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that is not -- that is not -- let me try to explain again. Mr. Enver Dziho, which is victim P in the expert report, and let me first explain what's written here in the expert report is the information that we provided to the expert, that sentence you just read out. Now, victim P, which is Enver Dziho, is the person who got wounded and which is under number 1 on the sketch -- or number 2 on the sketch. Then Mr. Stojan Kacic put Mr. Enver Dziho on a stretcher and moved Mr. Enver Dziho towards the ambulance, moved him up to the mountain towards -- up the mountain towards the ambulance. And while moving Mr. Enver Dziho on a stretcher, Mr. Stojan Kacic gets hit by a bullet, and it's in fact this particular incident that was seen by this witness, and that's the incident we're talking about here. So the sketch what -- what is drawn here, it stops at the fence but, as you can see on the video, from the fence onwards it again moves up. So this sketch should not be confused with what we later see on the video. I hope I've made myself clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I think some of the confusion, Your Honour. It's certainly quite clear from the sketch on the expert report that he's talking about victim Q. He says that on -- Lieutenant Van Der Weijden says that. Possibly some of the confusion stems from the practical schedule that the Prosecution gave a few weeks ago, but I think maybe the wrong victim got in front of me, maybe the wrong victims on that schedule. But if Your Honours treat that schedule, which we had a couple of weeks ago, with a bit of caution, because time's moved on, then the position seems to be clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, could you just -- could I just ask you to make a line from where Mr. Enver Dziho was put on a stretcher and the trajectory which was then followed towards the place where you actually saw Mr. Stojan Kacic being shot at.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And maybe you can mark with an X where you actually saw Mr. Stojan -- Mr. Stojan Kacic being -- being shot.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Here there's a concrete wall behind the house, and here behind the wall, this is where I was, and this is where I took shelter, and then I followed their way until they got to the very top of the staircase. Ibro was the first on the stretcher, and then I could hear a shot. Stojan Kacic grabbed his foot and then came down the stairs close to me to seek shelter as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you maybe put on this drawing the stair -- staircase where Mr. Stojan Kacic was being shot. Could you draw that on this sketch as well.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a street. This is the top of the staircase, and Ibro was almost at the top of the staircase. Kacic was below him by the full length of the stretcher. That's how further down he was. This is approximately the place where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If we could now then play the -- continue the video again, and I'll ask again the video to be stopped and then I'll ask you a few more questions. Yes. Maybe, Witness, would you mind putting your initials on the bottom of this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And if I could get an IC number for this sketch, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this will be IC 389.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could now continue the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: "Investigator: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, could you please walk the path that two paramedics followed carrying the body of Enver Dziho on a stretcher, and could you stop at the spot where the paramedic Stojan Kacic was shot. "Witness: [Witness complies]"

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If we could stop the video over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, we just saw the whole video and there was no sound. Do you recall what questions you were asked while standing over here?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was asked to say where Kacic was standing and where he was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what did you answer to the question where he was hit?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was standing at the place where Mr. Kacic had been standing before me, and I pointed with my hand. I can't remember which leg it was. I believe it was his right leg which had been hit, and he could not walk on that leg. That's when he started descending to the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did the investigator also ask you to point the exact location where Mr. Kacic was actually hit, in the video. So not on the body but the location on the stairs. Did the investigator ask you that? And is it correct that the investigator then made a yellow cross on that particular location?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That's it for the video, Your Honours. I would now like to show the witness the 360 photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, before you, you see a photograph, and again, this is a photograph that you were also shown. Is it correct that you were shown this photograph this morning as well?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that we went through the whole photograph, which makes a 360-degree turn, and that I asked you to stop on the position where you think that the shot came from that hit Mr. Kacic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What we'll do now is we'll again make a turn, and I will again ask you to say "stop" when we get to the position where you think Mr. Kacic was hit.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, we made a video still of this particular position where I would like you now to look at, and we'll put that on the overhead projector. And could I ask you to mark on this photograph where you think the shot was fired from?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe you can use the marker and put a circle around this.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, you've marked a circle around a tall buildings. Do you know the name of this building?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is the Privredna Banka building, a building that had not been finished by that time. It is otherwise known as the "glass bank" because it's made of glass. It's a glass construction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And what makes you think that the shot came from this particular building?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Because it is high up above other buildings, and there's a clear view from it. There's a line of vision, a clear line of vision from that building. And very good protection for anybody who shoots from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, I have a few more questions about this photograph. Right underneath your marking we see an orange coloured roof of a house. Is this house already there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: The -- the upper floor was not there. It was just a ground floor of a very old house, and I suppose that the owner in the meantime has been given a donation of money to finish the house. So the upper floor was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And then on the right-hand side of the photograph, we see a grey concrete wall. Was this particular wall, was this already there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't there. The building is my neighbour's workshop. He is an entrepreneur, and he has built a workshop and a storage to keep his tools and things in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: If you could again put your initials on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And if I could get an IC number for this particular photograph, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 390.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, there's one thing in your statement I want to ask you a couple of questions about, and I want to briefly show you a few more documents and then I'll be done. On page 3 of your statement, you say that it was also common for sniper to shoot at people up the street which was exposed to the glass bank building. My question in relation to this testimony is, how did the presence of snipers affect you and the other people in East Mostar in your daily life in 1993? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: In my view, sharpshooters were more dangerous than shells themselves, because a shooter could see you, could see your body, could see your face. A shell may fall anywhere, with a target or without a target, whereas a sharpshooter shoots with intention. He sees the body. He sees a face, and he shoots creating panic. And in my view, snipers were much more dangerous than shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But how did the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: My question is: How did the snipers affect the daily life of the persons living in East Mostar? How did it affect you personally when you would go on the streets or in your daily life in Mostar in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Those who had to go somewhere risked their lives if they did so in daytime. Most of our life and activities took place during the night. That's when things were taking place. And it had a psychological impact on us. We were afraid, and we lived with the feeling that you were some -- always targeted. You were afraid for your family, for your children, for your own life.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could I lastly ask you to look at the documents in this bundle, which is Exhibit 6263 and 8457.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can help you. You first have the English version and then behind it the original B/C/S version. Witness, is it correct that these two documents, I showed you these two documents this morning as well?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And is it correct that these are medical documents relating to Enver Dziho, and that both documents state that the date of injury was the 30th of October, 1993? Now, witness, in your statement you don't recall the exact date that this particular incident occurred, but if it says here the 30th of October, 1993, would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes my examination. I would just want to mention that as far as Mr. -- as far as Mr. Stojan Kacic is concerned, we have an entry of this person in one of the war hospital protocol books, which is Exhibit 05853, and there he is recorded also on the 30th of October for treatment of a bullet wound. That concludes my examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have a very short question to put to you. We know that you were a driver in the firemen's brigade, or in the firemen unit, and as far as I can understand, you were recruited as a fireman after you were discharged from Heliodrom on 24 July, 1993. While you were a fireman, did it ever happen to you to go to certain places to secure people who had been wounded by sniper? For example, in this particular cases when we're talking about Stojan Kacic, you have told us about that, but was that the only case or were you ever called to other places to help other victims as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only on one other occasion was I an eyewitness. The name of the person was Uimo Zer [phoen]. He was my colleague. He was shot and two or three days later he succumbed to his wounds. We were together. We were repairing tyres. He was also a member of the fire -- fire brigade unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the translation in my own language, but I've been following the transcript, and you said that there was another occasion when this happened, when you witnessed such a case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the second time one of your colleagues was hit. So these were the only two interventions that you had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now, Defence, you have three-quarters of an hour. Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Following Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for the witness on part of the Defence for Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. President and Your Honours. We also have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Praljak will have a few questions which your leave, but just for the record, I would like to repeat the name that we did not hear. This is incident under item 14, and the name that the witness mentioned was Uzeir Jugo. We already dealt with this incident, and he is therefore making a reference to an incident that we already are familiar with, not any other incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I will start with Ljubo Uzeir. You said you were repairing tires together; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Where was that? Was it in the courtyard of the firemen brigade's perimeter or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: It was in the perimeter of the firemen's brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's repeat that. The courtyard -- as we enter from Brace Brkica Street through the gate, there is a courtyard.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not there. The first courtyard. Not behind the building but the front yard, in front of the entrance into the firemen's building where two lorries could be parked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So not the inner courtyard?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not the inner one, in front of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So in the middle of the street then?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When Stojan Kacic, who was hit, he was carrying the stretcher with Enver Dziho who had been wounded before?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Was it -- was he carrying the front part of the stretcher or the back part of the stretcher?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: The back part.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You don't know in which leg he was hit?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I assume that it was his right leg.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Where in his right leg?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he grabbed his upper leg with his hand. Maybe he did not touch the place where he was wounded. Maybe his whole leg hurt and was not functioning properly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was his right leg.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We don't have any proof from the Prosecution as to what the wound looked like, where he was hit, whether it was his right leg or his left leg, whether it was his lower or upper leg. I have another question, Witness. When Enver Dziho was hit, he was, at least in your drawing, in front of a house.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: In front of a -- a garage or a storage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And in front of that house there is something that is known in Mostar as a library in the Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but that is a bit further, some hundred metres away in that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But when you stand in the place where Enver Dziho was hit, from that building in the library building do you see the glass bank were you ever in this that place did you ever turn to the that place were you able to see the glass bank or whether the library building, which was in Marsal Tito Street, this allows you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: It has been told here that I found Dziho when he was already wounded, and as you're looking from that building you can see the glass bank despite the bank [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But not from the place where Mr. Dziho was wounded?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: There are no obstacles between the place where he was wounded and the bank. Between number 2 where Dziho was lying and the glass bank, there are no obstacle the barring the view.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We saw that the passage is dark.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: It is a shadow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, it -- it was a shadow. In narrow streets when the weather is good and it is sunny, it is always dark. There is shadow. Can you now imagine that from the glass bank which is 700 or 800 metres away? One could see either with a pair of binoculars or without them. Could you see a person walking through any of these dark little alleys in your view?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the picture tells one thing and in real life is a different thing. I believe that, despite the sun, one would could see things very clearly. I believe that in the picture, the shadow is more visible than in real life.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That's your opinion. Until we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the date when Mr. Kacic was wounded, do you remember what the weather was like? Was it sunny? Was to cloudy? Do you remember what the weather was like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was warm. It was summer. It was sunny. It was beautiful weather.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Regardless of the documentation, in your statement you said this sentence that I'm going to read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, there is another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Praljak. Just a follow-up on the President's question. Witness, it was warm and bright. What you say in your statement is that the two witnesses wore military clothes. Is that correct? Do you remember that? Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me put it this way: Muslims had been expelled from the eastern bank to the western bank at the beginning of the war. They didn't have anything. They were handed after the conflict with the BiH army they were again expelled to the west bank, and they wore anything they had, that they could get hold of. So there a was lot of colourfulness in people's attire. Some people would wear half of their clothes; would be civilians. The other half would be military. And, for example, there were people working on a construction site dressed in military uniforms. It was October. I don't remember the -- the exact date, and people wore anoraks and jackets working on construction sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the question put to you by my colleague was very precise. My colleague and I myself, and I believe my other colleagues, would like to know whether Mr. Kacic and Mr. Dziho wore an attire that, seen from 700 metres, could have made the person at that distance believe that they were BiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never looked through a sniper, and I don't know how people looked through some sniper sites, but I believe that one could make a distinction between a civilian and a person carrying a stretcher, be they a soldier or not. It is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you can remember, Mr. Kacic and Mr. Dziho, as far as you can remember, what did they wear? What did they have on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found Dziho lying down in a military shirt. I don't know whether he was just covered with that shirt or whether he actually wore it. And I remember that he wore civilian trousers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that he had a military blouse, a military shirt, which means that it was a camouflage shirt.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was a camouflage shirt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Barakovic, can you remember at what time of the day this happened? Was it in the morning, at lunchtime, in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous night I had been working. We were working 24 hours and then had a rest 24 hours. So I came back home from work, and I lay down to have a rest because it was very strenuous work. And then my wife told me that Dusanka Begovic, the neighbour next door, had been wounded. So I got up, went out to help, crossed over, ran across the place where this -- to the place where this happened because it was nearby. When I went down there I didn't see Dusanka, I saw Dziho Enver lying down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I know that. My question was what time approximately was this? Was it at 9.00, at 10.00, at 12.00, at 2.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the morning. Probably in the morning. I don't know what I actually went to sleep, what time it was, but it was morning, 9.00, 10.00, thereabouts. I don't really remember. There was no electricity. We had nothing, so we couldn't really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me at what time the video was taken? Was that also in the morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Possibly, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have no idea at what time of day you met with the investigator?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You just asked -- answered half my question. As far as Mr. Dziho is concerned, we knew that he -- know that he was wearing a camouflage top, but what about Mr. Kacic? What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, he had camouflage trousers, some old ones washed out, and he had a civilian shirt, a civilian top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now when you answered my colleague's questions you added another element, and I can't just skip over that. You explained that in the morning, because you were sleeping since you had been working round the clock previously, you had had a difficult day, your wife told you that the neighbour had been wounded, and that's how you came to get up. And then you said that it was the Begovic person who had been wounded, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dusanka Begovic, yes, a lady.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand correctly, in just a few minutes there were three people who were wounded; is that right? Because you said, "When I went out thinking that I would find Dusanka Begovic, I saw the other two wounded people." Or, rather, you saw Dziho, who had been wounded. So in the space of just a very short time, there are at least three people who had been wounded. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I woke up to go and help Dusanka, I went to the shelter -- to take shelter under the first house, and my second attempt to reach the wounded person was the -- my wife had told me that Dusanka was wounded, and I couldn't see Dusanka anywhere. I saw Dziho. Now, after that Mr. Kacic was wounded, and while they were waiting for the stretcher to come -- well, it -- the stretcher came. They took Dziho up, and how much time passed by I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Dziho and Mr. Stojan, were they both members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, do you know, since you were in the vicinity, did you know or do you know that behind the library building there was a mortar position of the BH army, the BH army had a mortar position?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: When I came to the fire brigade there wasn't a mortar there. There was no heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You never saw a mortar behind the library on Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You said when all the Muslims were expelled from the west bank to the east bank, do you know that the number of Muslims on the west bank throughout the war was never less than 7.000? Of course, I don't deny possible expulsions and so on. I don't say that nobody was expelled and that people didn't do what they did, but do you know, and you are an inhabitant of Mostar yourself, that the number of Mostars [as interpreted] who remained on the west bank throughout the war, never dropped below the figure of 7.000?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can give you my opinion but I haven't got any arguments there to put forward to bear that out. I would say far less people.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In your opinion, how many Muslims remained on the west bank?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Do I have to answer that question? I don't know. Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. You don't know. That's fine. Now, can we place this document on the overhead projector for the witness to look at. It is a photograph that you've already seen, witness, and you've marked the glass building, the glass bank on it. Would you mark on that photograph, once you've taken a look at it, some other buildings? Can you recognise where the Hotel Bristol was? Can we see the hotel from this angle?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Now, to the left above the red roof we see a building. What building is that? Do you think that that building is the building that is on the corner of the Bulevar running to Marsal Tito Street? It's also known as a bank building or Borovo building running to Spanish Square. Would you say that is the building where your finger is pointing to now?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it could be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Would you put a number 1 there, please. That's right.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Then there's a sort of hole, and then there's another building. Could that be the Bristol Hotel?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Bristol Hotel is opposite, towards the Neretva River, lower down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Looking at it from this angle, it should be to the left of the glass bank and to the right of the Borovo building. Would that make that white building the Bristol Hotel, do you think?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it could be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Then put a number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you are an inhabitant of Mostar, and you were also a fireman. So you know your area. Now, according to you, from the position where those people were wounded, the ones we mentioned a moment ago, if somebody happened to be located in the Bristol Hotel or in the Borovo building, for instance, could they see the three people who were wounded and -- well, actually, could they see the three people and shoot them, shoot at them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't pay attention to anything like that. I don't think I can answer your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher place this photograph on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But before that, would you place your initials on that photograph, the one next to you. Your initials, please. Put your initials on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Place your initials there. And, Madam Registrar, may we have a number for the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 391.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: This is the photograph taken by the expert, and we see the glass bank building and the Borovo building, and I think you can see the Bristol Hotel very well now, and a house below the glass house -- or glass building. So would you place number 1 at Borovo, number 2 at the Bristol Hotel. Let me repeat. Number 1 for Borovo. Left, above the roof. No, that ought to be the Bristol Hotel. Take a good look. That's Borovo. So put a 1 there. Now the Bristol Hotel. Number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And the glass bank, number 3. That's it.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A follow-up question, sir. You've just put a number 2 where the Bristol Hotel is. Now, I can note that it is in a straight line facing the staircase, the steps. What distance would you say as the crow flies is the hotel from the steps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps 300 metres, 3 to 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Three to 400 metres. Thank you. Now, sir, when the shots were fired did you know who was controlling the bank building? Whose -- under whose control was the bank building and the Bristol Hotel and Borovo? In whose hands? Do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your answer was yes. Who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO was in control of the bank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO controlled all three buildings, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The Bristol Hotel was on the BH army side, and the bank that was destroyed and Borovo was between the lines on the BH army side. The Bulevar was the separation line.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let me ask you more precisely. If the Bulevar was the separation line and the HVO was in the secondary school buildings, who was in the Borovo building?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I said the BH army and in Borovo, Bristol.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So the BH army was in control of Borovo and Bristol; right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now look at the buildings underneath the glass house or glass bank. They are houses there are nearer, nearer to where we're looking from.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The two buildings, were they under BH army control, the two buildings that I indicated?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: They were on this side, the BH army side. Between the bank and the separation line there was nothing. Everything had been destroyed. The department store had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Could you put a 3 and 4 -- or, rather, a 4 and a 5. Could you place the number 4 and the number 5 there. Four.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And the white -- the building that is whiter. Yes, that's a --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now behind each of these buildings, could somebody have fired from these buildings at this place here, from any one of those buildings? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can shoot from any elevation, not only from these three buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You're a man from Mostar. Where they were on the east, could they fire at any point on the opposite side and vice versa? Was that what it was like in theory?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. It was a town. Everybody could shoot at everybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So all this area to the left of Mostar, at any elevated point you could shoot on the right side and vice versa. Anybody on the right side at an elevation of any kind could have shot on the left side -- at the left side.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Witness. Now, can we have medical documents with entry/exit wounds and so on? Can we ask for that so that we can round off this subject of snipers without anybody having proved where the sniping came from and what actually happened before the expert witness comes in again? Could you put your initials on that photograph, Witness, please. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place your initials on the photograph, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Madam Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 392.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I asked the Prosecutor that by the time the expert comes in next time that he should provide us with medical documents or photograph or whatever show that we can see where each of these two victims was hit and what the wound was like, whether it was an entry/exit wound or whatever. That's what I asked for. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I've no questions. May I just comment while I'm on my feet in relation to what Judge Trechsel said? I think Your Honours will find if you look at the videos and the photographs, not now but with the benefit of the compass directions, one can see pretty reliably what time of day it was because we know which is west and I think Judge Trechsel and Your Honours will get some guidance from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one question. You started asking a question, but I don't think it was fully answered. I'll just take a minute of your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. You were asked about the beginning of that day when your father told you that Dusanka had been bit but when you went on the spot you saw Dziho. Now, can you say something about that in your statement? Can you just confirm? Now, as far as I understand it from your statement, Dusanka Begovic was in fact not hit. She was not hit at all, but you realised that later on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions but since Mr. Kovacic came back again, Your Honour, Mr. Petkovic would like to use a little time for a couple of questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I would like go to see IC 389, that sketch, please. May we see the sketch again, IC 389. May we lower it a bit? Can we see the top part? Now, Witness, would you mark the exact spot where the person was wounded, the man Stojan - what was his name? - where Stojan was wounded. The exact spot.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the length of the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You just mark the spot.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Spago was on the first step.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Place an X or whatever you like. And place an S for Stojan so that we know that is Stojan.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us where you were when Stojan passed by you and was wounded?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: There's a concrete wall here behind the house, so that's where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: There's an entrance on the upper storey and a concrete wall closing off the yard right below the steps leading up to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can put it on the roof, although you weren't on the roof.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying. It would appear as if I'm on the roof, whereas I was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Place an X there.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was to the right of the wooden fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And that would be number 4. Place a 4 there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: How far was that from Stojan?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: From Stojan to where I was? About 20 steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you walk behind him or did you run?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where Dziho was wounded, Ibro Spago told me, "Go and bring a blanket so that we can transport him to another place." And I came to this house here and that's where I stopped for me to be able to run across. However, in the meantime somebody present said the stretcher was coming because the institute of hygiene was close by. However, allegedly Dusanka had been wounded before that. That's what we heard. We heard that Dusanka had been wounded, and somebody who had been to the hospital had brought the stretcher, and they put Dziho Spago [as interpreted] on the stretcher. They came up to me and passed by me, and then I went behind them and crouched down behind the wall, and then the rest happened. They took him up there because the ambulance was up there. The ambulance couldn't come down to the other side. So the ambulance parked by the school up on the road, and then Dziho managed to pull out. There was a shop there, and anyway, he was pulled out and driven off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: And when he came back to you, Mr. Praljak asked you where he was wounded and you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that he held his leg. So probably he was hit in the leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you didn't ask the man, "Where have you been hit?" You didn't look at it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Why would I when the ambulance came to drive him away?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't come and fetch him. He came back to the house.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: The other --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. A minute or so. Dusanka we heard had been wounded. She'd already informed the people down there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the next day you talked to Ibro about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We saw each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ask him what had happened?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what could have happened? We assumed what could have happened. And it could have been worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement, and you said that the statement was correct today, that in August it was -- in October it was summer.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: I said I don't know what time it was, but the weather was very fine, and it seemed to be sort of summer weather. And autumn in Mostar can be the same as summer, nice and warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: You said it was before Christmas, and we know that Christmas is in December and that it was a very nice day, and then you say it was probably summer.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, might be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was a little surprised to see that summer was in October before December, before Christmas.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL BARAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for this witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence teams have completed their cross-examination. Is there any re-examination from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I'd like to thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That completes your testimony, Witness. I would like to thank you for having come to make your contribution on behalf of the Judges and myself, and I wish you every success in your future work and best wishes for your safe return home. It is 20 to 4.00. We're going to take a 20-minute break and reconvene at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 4.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session for a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Belkisa Berisa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your date of birth, madam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1955.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, have you got a current occupation or are you a housewife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a housewife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. A housewife. Now, would you go ahead and read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. You may be seated. We're going to take the screens away. Let me give you some information. To start off with the Prosecutor who you might have met with yesterday or this morning is going to ask you questions and maybe present you with documents, show you some video material and photographs, and that will be short. Then you will have the Defence counsel sitting to your left, and perhaps the accused, who will be asking you questions as well. The Defence has 45 minutes at its disposal, and we hope that the Prosecution will be able to get through the summary in 20 minutes pursuant to Article 92 bis or ter. If you have any difficulties, madam, please don't hesitate to let us know and we'll take a break, but tell us if you experience any difficulties. So that is how the proceedings are going to evolve. I'm going to gift floor to the Prosecution. I don't know who it is. Is it Mr. Mundis who is going to be taking the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Berisa.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, pursuant our usual practice, I'm now going to read the Rule 65 ter summary of the witness's expected testimony. The witness was a resident of East Mostar living in the area called Rodoc. On about 2 September, 1993, she and her family were expelled from their home by Croatian Defence Council soldiers. They were escorted by Croatian Defence Council soldiers who told them to walk towards Buna. Her husband, Ibrahim Berisa, was arrested by Croatian Defence Council soldiers and imprisoned in Heliodrom. The witness and her family went to East Mostar - excuse me - and stayed with relatives in the area of Tekija. On 2 February, 1994, her son Orhan Berisa, born 5 March, 1985, was killed by a sniper while playing outside in Tekija. That concludes the Rule 65 ter summary. I would ask with the assistance of the usher if the witness could please be provided with a bundle of documents. I see she already has a bundle of the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ms. Berisa, in 2001, did you provide a written statement to investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: How do you mean? In writing, a written statement? What do you mean by "written"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the investigator of the Tribunal meet with you in September 2001 and ask you questions?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the end of that question and answer session, through an interpreter, did the investigator read back the statement to you with the interpretation providing the statement to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, ma'am, if you would now turn to what's been marked P 09856. Do you have that document in front of you? And I ask you to please turn to the first page of that in the English. And I would ask you, ma'am, if you see your signature on this document.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did sign it. That is my signature. She read the statement to me, and I just signed it. And it's my story. It is my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Berisa, when you came to The Hague two days ago, were you provided with a Bosnian language version of your statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after being provided with a copy in the Bosnian language, ma'am, did you have an opportunity to read the statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Having read the statement in the Bosnian language, Mrs. Berisa, is there anything you would like to add to the statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: I read it. I don't want to add anything. I just want to tell the story. I want to tell what I wrote in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll get to that, ma'am, in just a moment, but let me ask you this: Is there anything that you would like to change with respect to your written statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is there anything that you would like to delete or take out of your written statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If I were to ask you a series of questions like the investigator did in 2001, would the answer to those questions be the same as what is written in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: It would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, ma'am, to the best of your recollection, is that written statement that you have before you truthful?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: It is truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time, Mrs. Berisa, that the investigator of the Tribunal met with you, did you provide him with some documents relating to your son Orhan?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please turn to 8501 in the bundle before you and tell us what the document 8501 is?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This is a death certificate, a death certificate. This is my son's death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask you, ma'am, if you could now turn to the Exhibit 9132, and if you could please tell us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This is another death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And does this document also relate to your son Orhan?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, Orhan Berisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would now ask, ma'am, if you could please turn to Exhibit 9045 [Realtime transcript read in error, "9405"] that is also in the bundle and tell us, if you can, please, what that document is.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. This one is a birth certificate, a birth certificate for Orhan Berisa, and the other one is a death certificate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Berisa --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript says 9405 I think it's 9045.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 9045, that is correct. Thank you very much, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisa, could you please tell us about the day that your son Orhan Berisa was shot?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: That day, around 1.00, I had prepared lunch for my children. Then my acquaintance, Elvira Husic, called me and said, "Belkisa, it seems that your son Orhan has been wounded in the leg." In the meantime I ran up to my cousin's balcony. I thought that I would see better and then my husband appeared and said, "Why are you going to the balcony? There's stairs here." But I couldn't see where I was going, and I was looking down below in front of the balcony. I could see my child lying on the ground near the balcony in the courtyard, and he only said, "Mother." I could throw just a quick glance at him, and then my husband drew me inside, and I never saw him again after that, and I -- I felt unconscious. That was the last time, the last time when I saw my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisa, I'm sure everyone would understand if we need to take a break for your benefit and so, if that's the case, please --

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you do need a take a break at any point in time, ma'am, you tell us, and we'll take a break for your benefit. Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Thank you. No, it's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, at the time when you were making the lunch for your children that you told us about, where was your son Orhan at that point in time, and what was he doing while you were making the lunch?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: My son was in the basement where children were playing games. He was playing with them, and then he went outside to come upstairs to have lunch. But as he was passing through the courtyard there were sniper shots, and near the staircase of the other building he was shot through the back, and his whole body was shattered as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Berisa, can you tell the Trial Chamber how you found out what happened to your son? Who told you about this?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Elvira called me and told me, "Belkisa, Orhan is wounded in the leg," and I didn't know anything about him being wounded in the back. I thought he would be wounded in the leg. And then my husband came and, "Our Orhan is gone. He died on the spot where he had been shot." And then after that for a long time they didn't dare tell me the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisa, were you aware of the presence of snipers in Mostar in 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't dare go anywhere during the day. We didn't dare go and fetch water, and children did not dare go out and play. They would play in the basements. He was only young. He didn't know, or he thought It wouldn't be me. We just could not make it clear to the children it wasn't safe and they were not supposed to play outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
