utterances.text: Mrs. Berisa, do you know based upon your discussions with your neighbours and other people who lived in your building where the snipers were located in Mostar or in the vicinity near your apartment building?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Of course I do. There were hundreds of them, hundreds, and we had to be aware of the hundreds of them. And there -- there was this place called Stotina where they were. And not only my child. There was another child who was a refugee, and another girl who lived in the neighbourhood, and my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now -- Mrs. Berisa, I'm going to show you a photograph on the computer screen in front of you. It's a 360-degree photograph like we looked at earlier today. I'm going to show this photograph to show the entire 360-degree circle, and after we're done with that I'm going to ask you some questions. Do you understand that, Mrs. Berisa?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm going to rotate the photograph all the way around in a complete circle and then I'll ask you some questions at the end. Now, Mrs. Berisa, do you recognise what was visible in this 360-degree photo that I've just shown you?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This is the place where my son got killed, the late Orhan, near the staircase where you came out of the basement through the door of the other building. He ran up to the other building, and this is where he was hit in the back from Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now, ma'am, with the assistance of the usher some photographs can be shown to you, and I'm going to ask you if you can make some markings on these photographs, which are stills that were taken from the 360-degree photo that we just saw. The photograph that's now -- that you're now looking at, ma'am, can you tell us what this photograph is a picture of?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Here, this is where my son got killed, my young son. Below this staircase, this is where he was crawling through, and then there were some other children, two neighbour's children that dragged him through to the other building, and this is where he got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Berisa, can you please take that marker that you have, and I'd ask you to draw an X at the location where Orhan fell when he was shot.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned this is where he was crawling through. Can you draw a line in the direction that you were just pointing to with the pen? Can you please draw a line indicating --

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Up to here. Up to below this balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, we can see, ma'am, the staircase and -- and the area that's underneath the balcony. Can you tell us, the line that you've drawn does it go up the stairs, or does it go behind the stairs, under the balcony?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Below the stairs. Below the balcony. This is where children went, and this is where they caught him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now the usher to provide you with a second photo. In the meantime, Mrs. Berisa, could you please put your initials on that photograph for me, the one that you've just marked. Yes. And we would ask for --

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: I didn't understand. What do you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please just put your initials down on the bottom of that photograph.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a question. Leave the photo, please. First of all, can we have an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 393.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, a little bit more about this photo. Witness, I have to ask you something to clarify a certain thing that you said. We have here a hill or a mountain, and behind, across the road from the hill, what is there? Are there any buildings? Or what is there? We can't see it in this particular photo. We can see the mountain or the hill, but what is across from it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you referring for this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the hill.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Stotina, but this building did not exist at the time. This is a newly built building. This was empty here, this area here. And this is Stotina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but if you look at the hill called Stotina, behind your back, what would be there? Another mountain, another hill, a building? If you were facing Stotina, what is behind your back?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: There's just Stotina here. There's no other hill. This is Stotina, nothing else, no other hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Judge, perhaps if -- it might be helpful I have three more photographs to show her and then perhaps we could show the 360 again, and it might then become a little bit clearer to Your Honour, if perhaps we can just proceed like that if that's okay. Could the second photograph now be shown to Mrs. Berisa. Now, you told us, ma'am, a few moments ago that your son -- or the other children were crawling under the balcony. Can you tell us what's advisable in this photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This is the balcony. Below the balcony children were crawling, and they brought my child to in front of the other building here, and this is where I saw him. This is what children explained to me. Here below the balcony, over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Mrs. Berisa, could you again take the marker and draw what you've described as under the balcony to the place out -- where your son was taken out.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, again, ma'am, for purposes of clarification, you've drawn the line right below the handrail. Was that where your son was, or was he under that platform?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Below. Below.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you see, ma'am, the corner of that platform in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Again, I didn't understand your question. I apologise. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see where the two lines that you've drawn cross, where they intersect?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: The other one comes here. This is where it is supposed to come through from the courtyard, and this here is a car. So from this car here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me make sure that we all understand, because the lines that you've drawn appear to be up on the stairs. Is that right, where you've drawn the line?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: But under the balcony. This is under the balcony. This is below, but this is through the middle. This here is empty. This is an empty space.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to understand. The empty space below where you've drawn the lines, is that where your son was taken out?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, it's empty below. Yes, yes. This is where it's empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please take the marker and colour in the empty area below. Can you see the empty area in the photo?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just please shade that area in or colour that area in with the marker.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now where you've drawn the squiggly line, is that where your son went out -- was taken out?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, through here, underneath, below this concrete thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, again, Mrs. Berisa, if you could please place your initials in the bottom right-hand corner of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And we would ask that this also be given an IC number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes IC number 394.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, Mrs. Berisa, to look at two more photographs. First we'll look at this one. Can you tell us what's depicted in this photograph, please?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This photo depicts the basement. From this basement my son ran up to the staircase, and this is where he was shot from Stotina. From the basement he ran up. He was running up to the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me say -- let me ask you this, ma'am. When you say the basement, which -- can you circle what you say is the basement, or from this -- you say this photo depicts the basement. Can you circle what you mean by the basement?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: The basement is inside. How am I supposed to -- this is the basement. This is the basement window, and this here is the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this, then, ma'am: There's a door that's open. Do you see the open door?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the open door, and this is the basement under the entire building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you went through the open door, Mrs. Berisa, where would you end up? Where would you go if you went through that door?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Down the stairs to the basement, up the stairs to the apartments in the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you please place an X on the doorway that would lead into the building where you could either go down into the basement or up in the apartments.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: But this entrance door is the same for the building, for the apartments and for the basement. It's the same door. There's just one door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand, ma'am. Could you just for the record place an X on the door, the doorway.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us that your son was in the basement playing while you were making the lunch. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, to go from the basement to your apartment, what was the route your son would have taken?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This would be the route, and then he should have entered under the staircase, and then he would have entered our building. I just pointed those to you a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mrs. Berisa, at the end we'll show the 360 again and you can explain it perhaps to the Judges, having marked these photos. Can you please draw a line from the X, an arrow, if you would, from the X the direction your son would have gone to your apartment.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Are you referring to this here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mrs. Berisa, if you could please put your initials on the lower right-hand corner of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that it be given an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes IC number 395.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And finally, Mrs. Berisa, in terms of the photographs, in response to a question from one of the Judges a few moments ago you mentioned a house that wasn't built at the time your son was shot. Do you see that house in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you -- can you trace the outline of that house, including the roof, with the red pen for us, please?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Berisa. Do you know when that house was built, approximately, the house that you've just circled?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Maybe three years ago. Three and a half, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, what is on the opposite side of that house? What is behind that house? What would you be able to see if that house weren't there?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: There's nothing behind the house but a park, and behind the park you can only see Stotina, nothing else. There's a road, a street. I don't know how to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So before this building was build could you see the Stotina house or not? Could you see the houses in Stotina or could you not before this house was built?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, you could see them or yes, you could not see them?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: You could see the houses, and the house us still stand there. They've always been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I Would ask, ma'am, that you would put your initials on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would also ask that it be given an IC number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 396.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now I'm going to show you, ma'am, if you could now please look at the 360-degree photo on the screen. We're going to go through that one more time, and again, because we've now marked the photos, you can just describe for us what you see on the 360-degree photo. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So when you see something that you'd like to tell us about, please do so, and I'm going to start rotating the photograph now. Ma'am, we're not able to capture it, so if there's anything you want to say, please say so rather than -- I don't know. It appears as though you might be pointing. If there's anything you'd like to say as we show this one last time.

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Here, that's where the space underneath the balcony is. I'll show you where the children were going up the stairs. So underneath that balcony there, and then two children came to help my child and pulled him out. This is an entrance to the building, 9C, number 9C. This is where this was sawed -- sawed off so they could go up and down, and they would jump down from there. And that's where the entrance is where you go to my building where I was with my relatives. That's the building. That's where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Berisa, at the time of your son's death, how old was he?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: He was to have a birthday and be nine years old in 23 days' time. He was too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, Mrs. Berisa, could you please turn to 9046 in the bundle that you have in front of you. Can you tell us, ma'am, how old your son was when this photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you for answering our questions, Mrs. Berisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, as far as I'm concerned in these very dramatic and painful times, I nonetheless have to do my job and ask you some questions in order for the Judges to have all the elements necessary for us to be able to know and realise what happened. You said on several occasions that the shot came from Stotina, and we have the photograph in front of us where behind the house built three years ago there's the hill and there are houses behind there. Now, in February 1994, and in January, to the best of your knowledge, madam, had there already been shots which had wounded or killed people in the area that we can see depicted on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So your answer to my question is yes. Now, all the inhabitants, did they know that the area was very, very dangerous? Did all the residents know that?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what about the parents, the fathers and mothers of the children like you? Did they tell their children to be very, very careful when going out into that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I assume that's what -- that that is what you did. You explained to all your children that they should be careful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When your son was killed under the circumstances which you have described to us, did you yourself or your husband had or your family members, did they contact the BH army to ask why this had happened? Did you make any inquiries with the authorities if there were any authorities to be contacted at that time? Did you inquire what had happened, why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't ask anybody anything. I was very ill. My husband had been wounded. We had nobody to ask. We couldn't ask anybody anything. All we know is that the UNPROFOR people went out to the spot and took pictures, and the woman, Gas Sabaha, who took him to hospital, told me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling us that UNPROFOR came on the spot to take photographs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Not the spot, but my late son in hospital, in the institute of hygiene. They went to take photographs of him. That's what the lady told me, but I didn't see any of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, madam, to the best of your knowledge, in February the ABiH, did it have any soldiers in that area, in the buildings? Were there BH soldiers in your sector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't see any. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw and I heard -- you say that your husband was wounded. Under what circumstances was he wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992, my husband was wounded. He worked in the parks. He was cleaning the parks, and a shell fell, and he was wounded in his -- on his -- the left side of his body. A shrapnel entered in the heart area, and his arm -- the muscle of his arm was shattered, and he can't do a thing with his arm any more. So he was wounded -- he was wounded very seriously, and he's an invalid from that shell that exploded. That was in 1992. It was in July, August when he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: The authorities in your country, I assume that in Mostar there was a prosecutor. Now, to the best of your knowledge, the authorities in your country, did they undertake an investigation to find out what had happened? Did you yourself -- were you yourself called to give testimony, or did you see any lawyers or did nobody bother about you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody ever bothered to come and see me, no lawyer, nobody. Nobody came to ask about our pain and suffering, the suffering of a father and mother losing a child like that. I didn't see anybody, hear anybody, talk to anybody. Nobody came to ask us anything. I can say that quite definitely. I can say that under oath anywhere. Nobody came to tell us what had happened or to ask what happened, whenever --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I assume that in Mostar today you're not the only person who had a child killed or wounded or whose nearest and dearest had suffered in some way, and is it really true that none of the authorities are investigating, gathering information about those incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't know about that. Only the social centre that has the records. That's the only place, but nobody else anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Madam, do you know by whom your husband was wounded, from which side, from Serbs, from HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The former army. The Serbs. The beginning it was. That was at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Hvala Ljepo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your husband, having been wounded by the Serbs, he doesn't receive an invalid's pension, a disability pension, or any subsidies or financial support and assistance of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He couldn't receive anything. Nor does he have any money or anything. No remuneration at all because my husband wasn't a soldier. He was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has 45 minutes. Who is going to start off?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Prlic has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We have no questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just have one question with respect to a photograph to link it up with the expert witness later on. May I have IC 396 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam. I am adjust going to ask one thing to help us out with that photograph. I won't bother you with any other questions. Just tell us, please, to the left of the building that you've marked, the building to the left, did that building exist during that terrible tragic event when your son was killed?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: To the left. That building. That's right. Did -- was that building in existence?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So it was only this other building that you marked with a circle that was built later?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes. This area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So all the other buildings that we see on the photograph were in existence at that time?

utterances.speaker: BELKISA BERISA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No questions from the Petkovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no questions either, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis. Thank you. Madam, that completes your testimony. On behalf of my colleagues and myself, I would like to express all our sympathies for the drama that you lived through. All I can advise you to do is perhaps see a lawyer in Mostar if you have the means to do so, and perhaps try and find out what exactly happened, and also to receive some psychological support and assistance. Before, of course, it is only a lawyer who can advise you what to do. Now, the Victims and Witness Unit might also be able to help. And all that remains for me to do is wish you a safe journey back to your country, and we express our condolences. I'm now going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you for listening to me, for hearing me out so I could express my pain somewhere and before someone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This brings us to the third witness of the day. Any protective measures requested there?

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there are no protective measures requested, but I would just caution one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: The witness's statement is going to be tendered under Rule 92 ter, as Your Honour will know. In that statement, on the last page, there is mention of a particular incident, and I may therefore be tendering the statement under seal and would appreciate if anything pertaining to that particular incidents were not mentioned in open court as it may seek to identify another person rather than this witness, being the concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That relates to the last three paragraphs, does it, of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be good practice for a redacted version to go public, seeing as most of the statement relates to this particular incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Indeed. The Prosecution is more than happy to redact as the Chamber wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to place it under seal for the time being. Then you can provide a redacted version after which we can give it a definite number. I'm going to ask Madam Usher to go and fetch the witness. We're going to take a break at around 5.30. I hope, Ms. Gillett, that you'll be able to complete your examination in 30 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I hope so, too, Your Honour. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness seems to have disappeared. We're going to take a break to be able to find the witness and reconvene in 20 minutes' time at 5.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Let me just check to see whether you can hear me and understand me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have your first and last name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Elvir Demic, the 2nd of October, 1970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your currents occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I work as a professional firefighter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sir, have you ever testified before a tribunal on the events that took place in your country or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you now go ahead the read the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some information to start off with. You've already met the Prosecution. They're going to ask you some questions and show you some documents, and the Prosecution will have about 20 minutes to do that. After that, the Defence counsel and the accused will have 45 minutes at their disposal to ask you questions if they consider that necessary, and the Judges sitting before you might also be asking you questions. If at any time you're feeling unwell, don't hesitate to let us know. So that, in general terms, is how the proceedings are going to be conducted. And if everything goes ahead as scheduled, you'll be finished with your testimony by the end of the day. Madam Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. Thank you. I'll begin by reading a brief summary of the witness's statement which will be duly tendered into evidence under Rule 92 ter. The witness was a member of the fire brigade in East Mostar. The firemen and the fire trucks were targeted by the HVO artillery and snipers when attending fires. Around September, 1993, the witness was attending a fire in East Mostar when the firemen were targeted by HVO mortars and snipers. As a result, they were forced to withdraw from the fire. When things calmed down, they tried to return to the fire but were again targeted by a sniper. Several bullets hit the water tanker that they were in, and one bullet entered the cabin and grazed the back of the driver's head. The wounded driver was Alija Jakupovic. That concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember being interviewed by somebody from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: It was in 2001, sometime during the summer.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, at that time when questions were put to you, did you answer the questions truthfully?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And did you do so voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: At the end of the interview do you recall the statement being read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And at that time, do you recall signing the statement that had been prepared confirming to the best of your knowledge and recollection that it was true?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness be shown the B/C/S and English versions of his statement which are marked as Exhibit 09857.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, have you had the opportunity to read this statement again prior to coming into court, either today or yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if you look through the statement, both the English and B/C/S versions, is that your signature or your initials that we see on each of the pages?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Having re-read the statement, is there anything that you would wish to withdraw or delete or to correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And today do you still stand by the contents of the statement as being true to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: The Prosecution will tender the statement in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to your statement, you mention on the first page of the statement that the fire trucks were red fire trucks, and yet a little later on when we get to view a video, you mention a yellow fire truck. What I'd like to ask you is whether there was any difference between red and yellow fire trucks.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: The fire brigade's vehicles were all red. Now, why this particular one was yellow, the sole reason was that before it reached the firefighters' union, it had been used in the utilities company. It was used for washing the streets and washing the parks and so on. Now, when the conflict broke out, since we were lacking in vehicles and in fire engines, I don't remember how that truck came to be in the fire brigade but, anyway, it came to the fire brigade. And as it was wartime, we didn't have an opportunity to paint it red, so it stayed yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: How many yellow fire trucks were there in the fire brigade at that time?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, just that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: A little later on in your statement, at page 3, you describe attending a fire at a house in September of 1993 in that particular yellow truck. You mention that there were several single shots impacting on the wall outside. Do you know what was being used to fire at you?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Of course I know. As a matter of fact, at that point we knew what types of weapons were in question because we were experiencing single shots with a very strong impact. This was sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, in 2004 do you remember meeting with an investigator and also a photographer from this Tribunal in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And at the time, were you asked a series of questions that related to the incident described in your statement in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And was this question and answer session videotaped?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I could ask the witness to be shown Exhibit 9140.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'm going to ask you if you would view the video that is going to be shown you, and I will ask you some questions following that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Demic, to the best of your recollection, is this the original yellow fire truck in which your colleague Alija Jakupovic was shot at in September 1993? "Witness: Yes. "Investigator: Has this truck now been painted red? "Witness: [Interpretation] Yes. "Investigator: Mr. Demic, to the best of your recollection, please indicate where bullets hit the truck on that day in September, 1993. "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you very much. Mr. Demic, to the best your recollection, could you please point where the bullet that hit Mr. Alija Jakupovic at the back of his head impact the truck? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you very much. Mr. Jakupovic, to the best of your recollection could you please assume the position in which you were when you were shot in the summer of 1993? "Witness: [Witness complies]. "Investigator: Could you please point out where the bullet hit you? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if Ms. Gillett realises we can hear her. She probably doesn't want to be heard when she's having those discussions with her own team.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I can appreciate that I can be heard. There's nothing secretive in what I was saying. The video does continue a little further, and I was hoping that we can, yes, get a little bit further along with the video. There is a short break from what we've seen and then it continues with this same witness in a slightly different location. I believe that we have now found that clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Demic, to the best your recollection could you please indicate where the fire truck was driving when it was shot at in September, 1993? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Mr. Demic, could you please point in the direction the fire truck was driving that day? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. Mr. Demic, to the best of your recollection could you point in the direction from which you heard the shots coming from? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, Witness, before I ask you any questions relating to the content of that video, I'd like you to confirm whether or not you recognised yourself in that videotape.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And also whether, at the time, you understood the instructions that were put to you by the investigator that we see in the videotape.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And at the time, did you comply truthfully and to the best of your knowledge with the instructions that you were given?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, and having viewed the videotape again, would you like to change any of the answers that you provided back in 2004 to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: No. There is no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Once again, Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender that video in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Just in relation to what we've seen in the video, in fact the last clip that we saw where you seem to be standing by a patch of grass, you mention in your statement, on the third page, second to last paragraph in, I believe, both the English and Bosnian language versions, that there was an open spot that you had to cross in the truck in which you were travelling. How long in terms of distance was that open spot?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: About 150 metres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now, in addition, you also mention in your statement that the bullets that hit the water tank must have been fired from the west. Can you be more precise in your description of where those bullets came from?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I adhere by what I said at the time. All the shots that were fired at us while we were extinguishing the fire and while we were moving about, all these shots came from the western part of the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can you be any more specific other than stating in the western side?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I was referring to HVO positions, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, you also mention in your statement that Mr. Alija Jakupovic was hit in the back of his head. Do you know what injuries he sustained?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, the driver Alija Jakupovic was shot in the head, in the back of the head. The wound was serious but not as serious as some others. He was taken to the hospital and then he was discharged home. He still suffers consequences. He has very frequent headaches. He has not been disabled by the wound, but this is where the wound was, in the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, finally before I shown you a photograph, in your statement you mention at the time of this incident you went to extinguish a fire in a house at around 1300 hours. Are you able to say at what time the truck in which you were travelling and in which Mr. Jakupovic was shot, what time that occurred?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: It was around 1.00 when we were called to attend to the fire, and the shooting incident during which my colleague was wounded took place around 1500 or 1530 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: And again do you remember how far away in terms of distance you had travelled from leaving the house where you'd been trying to extinguish the fire?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: We didn't get very far from the house. We managed to negotiate some hundred or 150 metres from the house itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, after the videotape that we've just seen was made, did you, back in 2004, observe the photographer placing a tripod on the location where you had been standing and taking some additional photographs?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown the Exhibit 9139, the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Before the photograph is rotated, Witness, what I'm going to ask you to do is view the photograph, and it will be moved around in 360 degrees. Now, I'd like you to watch the screen as this is happening and say stop if you see the location where you believe the person or people who shot at Mr. Jakupovic were located at the time. Do you understand what I'm asking you to do?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: The photo is now going to be rotated through 360 degrees, and you just say stop if you see the location I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, obviously that photograph contains and lot of information, a lot of buildings, and we also see hillsides at the back. Can you describe to the Court the exact location, using that photograph, from where you believe the shot or shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: This is the complex of white buildings that are in the shape of a cascade.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: There's quite a number of white buildings that photograph. Are you able to say whether it's the white buildings to the left, in the centre, or to the right of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: To the right above the roof of the railway station. Above that are step-like white buildings ascending at first and then descending towards the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, a screen shot has been taken of this particular location, which I would be grateful if I could be assisted in passing to you, and if it could be put on the ELMO. It might then be a lot easier if you can, using the pen that will be given to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed with this, I wonder if I could just make an observation which does apply to a lot of this sort of evidence, which is the way the question was put is, "Can you describe to the Court the exact location using that photograph from where you believe the shot or shots were fired?" But what that question does is jump right over the essential prior point which is the basis for that belief, because that is fundamental. There's no point in going on to the next stage of marking where he says unless we have dealt with that absolutely critical first stage, and it's not a matter to be let for cross-examination. It's a fundamental matter in the presentation of the Prosecution's evidence on this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm more than happy to take on board that point, safe to say that in the statement which this witness has given and which will duly be tendered and has been appropriately identified, there is evidence as to why the witness believes the shots came from that particular direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I'd like to make an observation about the statement which is that in the sixth paragraph of the statement the witness says, "I shall make it clear when I am talking about what I saw, and I shall make it clear when I am talking about what I have heard from someone else." Now, without going into elaborate submissions, the statement certainly does not do that. I'm not blaming the witness, particularly, because those bits of statements are drafted for him. But precisely because no such distinction is properly drawn, it's absolutely critical that when the Prosecution take the opportunity of supplementing the written statement in this way, that they do it in the way that we have just submitted it should be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have heard what the lawyer has just said. What prompts you to say that the shots came from the step-like buildings? Is that your assumption, or are you deeply convinced that this was the case for a certain specific reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I am certain, because I was present. I was sitting in the lorry, shoulder to shoulder with my colleague who got shot. Another thing that I'm absolutely certain of, since I was born there some hundred, 200 metres away from that place and I slept there for days, my parents live there, I know from them and from my own personal experience that this is where shots came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We know that you were in the lorry. You've -- you've told us exactly where the lorry was. We have a photo that depicts Mostar in its entirety. There are several buildings in that photo, and if a shot came from anywhere in Mostar towards the lorry, the firemen's lorry, it could have come from various places, from the left, right. But how do you know? What allows you to say that the shots came from the right side of the photo where we can see step-like buildings? How can you be sure? What allows you to say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part here where the railway station is, this part here, there was nobody there. In this part here, in this part there was a -- sort of a no man's land where there was no activity, and this was the separation line. Here were HVO positions, and only from this part, from those buildings, could the shots have come. And since the shots came in an oblique line, it could not have -- they could not have come from this point here, because if the shots had come from this place, the bullets would have entered through the door. But since they came from the back of the lorry, it is only logical that the shots came from the right, from these buildings here or from the area in front of them. And anything behind the white buildings would have been too far many there was no separation line or any other line, although anything goes. Anything is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say everything is possible, I see a building in front of the railway station which has two storeys and a lot of windows. I don't know whether it was there at the time in 1993, but I would say that the shots could have come from that building as well, and it is aligned with the roof of the railway station. So I would say that the shots could have come from there as well, from that building. I believe that in your view the shots came from the building after the separation line, but the shots could have easily come from the building that was in the area under the control of the BiH, although this might seem far-fetched to you, but why not, just for the purpose of an academic exercise. That is also possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is possible, but it really doesn't make any sense at all, because this building in front of the cascade and everything behind, everything was under the control of the HVO, save for this little part in the left-hand side corner and the railway station. The railway station was empty. There was nothing there. Everything behind that roof is the line after which everything was under the control of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this incident, as well as all the others that you witnessed, are the investigations over? Did anybody collect the bullets or debris?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not carry out any investigation. We didn't search for any bullets or anything like that. It was -- it was wartime, and it just wasn't done. We didn't find anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps now that you have the photograph in front of you and have been referencing a number of different points, it might make things clearer if you are able to mark on that photograph the location or locations where the -- you believe the shots came from. If you need to do that by means of marking with an X, or if it's easier to draw a circle around if it's a larger area, whatever is the easiest and most precise way of identifying the area for you.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, I can't be precise when pointing to the window from which the shots came, but I am sure, and I assume, of course, that this would be this complex of buildings. There are some smaller houses that you can't see in -- in this area from the trees, but there are some smaller buildings there as well, and the shots could have come from there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I am looking at the photo of the lorry with a lot of attention, and you pointed your finger when you were with the investigator where the shots came from and where they entered, and you pointed to four holes, and you explained that there was a bullet that entered through the back of the lorry and entered in the head of your colleague. When I saw the photo and when I listen to you, the first impression I had was that the shots came from the round -- you -- you are a fireman. What was your impression when -- was the lorry targeted? Or the cistern, was it targeted to destroy the source of water, or was the driver of the lorry targeted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we arrived there to extinguish the fire we were rather successful, and the -- we were shot at as soon as we arrived. But we were protected at first. That's how the house was built. The lorry was not visible. And after that there was mortar fire. Some five or six shells were fired into the house and around the house. Until then, until we arrived there to tend to the fire, the day was peaceful and calm. As we started leaving the place of the fire, we started leaving in the lorry, and we could not have passed 50 metres or so. There were first shots at the lorry. The first shot, I don't know where it hit. It did hit the lorry because we heard the sound of metal. And then there was the second shot, the third shot. And the fourth shot was fatal because it hit our driver. As we were driving, we had to pass another 50 metres or so to the next house where we would have been safer. And I believe that a sniper shot is not strong enough to pierce the cistern metal because this is much thicker, and it can only scratch the surface of the metal. In addition to that, since the cistern was hit three times, the person who was shooting was not happy with the three shots into the cistern but continued shooting into the driver's cabin, and it is obvious what the purpose was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chronology of what you're saying -- well, you said something that might be of importance to us Judges. You said that that was a mortar shell, which allows us to assume that it was extremely difficult for you to put out the fire, which was your job. But when a mortar explodes or shoots, it makes a lot of noise. So did you wonder where this could have come from or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we didn't ask ourselves those kind of -- those questions. We were fully conscious of what was going on at the time in town, and we knew the mortars -- where the mortars and the projectiles came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you just said they come from a particular location. What place was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know where they came from, but I know that they came from the HVO positions in the west. But I can't tell you the exact locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, I only have one more question to ask you. You've already mentioned, when I asked you earlier, the approximate distance that you and your colleague were away from the house whose fire you had been trying to put out, and again I believe at line 81.4 you also mention the distance of approximately 50 metres that you had left the house before the shots were fired. With that in mind, is it possible to see in the photograph that you were shown earlier, the 360-degree photograph, is it possible to identify the house that you had attended to on that day to extinguish the fire? Is it shown in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that house on the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: In that case, I would ask you once again to do a similar exercise before, and as the photograph is moved through the 360 degrees, if you could shout "stop" at the point where you're able to see this house to which we've been referring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop there, please. Sir, apparently what we can see on this photograph, the countryside, is opposite to what we were thinking of before. Now, I can see that there are hills. Now the hypothesis that I'm going to put to you: Couldn't the shot have come from there as well, from that part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the entry wound, the bullet -- are the bullet entered the truck, you can see that it entered from -- well, had it come from the upper side, it would have hit me here in my head. But as it was my colleague who was killed, it came across me and hit the other person, whereas if it came from the opposite direction it would have been somebody sitting to my right who might have been hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the hills that we can see behind, were there any armed forces there, military units, soldiers, or was there nobody there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was where ordinary civilians lived, just the people, civilians. No soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Witness, again if you could keep a lookout for the house that you had attended and say "stop" at the point when you see the house in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I haven't got the image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: That helps. Do you see it in front of you now, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Still further on, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Again we see a couple of buildings in that particular photograph. To which house are you referring?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: That is the house, the front one, the one in front. Well, behind it is the big house. So between those two houses on the right, there's a small roof that can be seen, a small roof in between, between the front house and the house -- the bigger house at the back. You can see a little red roof. That's the house. So we took this road, then we came to the open space where the stone is. So it's just about a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I believe that's a clear description.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions to put to this witness or indeed exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions? A question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sir, I have a very simple question. Can you tell us approximately at what speed you were driving at that time? How fast or how slow did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Better to say how slow, because the truck was an old one, not in very good repair. So I don't suppose we went faster than 20 kilometres per hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have 45 minutes to go to 7.00. That makes it perfect timing. First Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Second Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with the Court's permission, Mr. Praljak would like to ask a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you only have nine minutes unless you've been given time by other Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They have given me more time, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's clarify some points first. At that time in Mostar, was there the HVO on one side of Mostar and on the other side it was the BH army? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Was part of a detachment of the Mujahedin from Konjic present in Mostar at that time? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that outside the BH army there were certain troops, certain forces which were called the MOS, Muslim forces led by Mr. Smajkic, in part?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Not in Mostar. Perhaps elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Just say whether you know about this or not.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your statement you say that all the Muslims from the right bank were expelled to the left bank. Now, I want to know whether you know that at that material time, the time you're referring to, on the right bank of Mostar under HVO control were -- there were about 3.500 Serbs and 7.000 Muslims. Do you know about those figures?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't remember mentioning any expulsions or anything like that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'll find that passage. Just let me take a moment. It is on page 3 of your statement. You say: "The war between the Bosnian Croats and Bosnian Muslims started on the 9th of May, 1993. All the Bosnian Muslims were expelled from western Mostar and had to relocate to East Mostar."

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I remember now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So it is on the basis of that statement of yours that I am asking you the following: Do you know that in -- on the west bank despite some tragic events that took place, there were nonetheless 7.000 Muslims left and 3.500 Serbs who went on living there?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I know a certain amount of Muslims remained, but as to the figures, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, everybody says a sniper shot. Now, how can you tell a sniper shooting? What do you mean by sniper? Do you know what a sniper is?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do because I was in the former army, the JNA. I was an infantryman and I had occasion to see a sniper. I didn't shoot from a sniper, but I did see what it looked like and others.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can we agree that it is a type of rifle of a certain calibre which has a scope or optic sites which bring the target close up? That's what it means?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So when you hear a shot, you don't know if it's a sniper or a rifle without a sniper device?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, you can't tell if a sniper is shooting with a scope or without a scope, but you know that it's a sniper.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's take the M-48 rifle. Whether it has an optic sight or not, it shoots the same way?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Or a Remington rifle with optic sights or without --

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Realtime transcript read in error, "JUDGE ANTONETTI: [Interpretation]"] Well, it doesn't target the same way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and speak one at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, we agree that there is a difference if there's a difference in calibre. So the difference is just in calibre, not whether it has an optic sight or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Stop there. At line 9 on page 87, it seems that I said something but let me underline I was not talking at all. I wasn't speaking at that precise line and time. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The yellow truck at that time wasn't a fire engine by virtue of its colour, was it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, not by virtue of its colour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So somebody might consider that a yellow truck was carrying petrol for the BH army and would have considered that to be a legitimate military target. Would you agree with me there? They could. It's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, at some point in time maybe, but not at this point in time. It was a truck. Let me explain to you. A truck which was transporting water cannot be carrying petrol. Now, somebody -- a truck carrying petrol can carry water. So the water trucks were just designed for carrying water and they haven't got many same valve system and all the rest of it. So if you were to pour petrol in it, the petrol would run out because it wasn't designed to carry petrol.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, I understand what you're saying, but put yourself -- place yourself in a position of somebody five or six metres away [as interpreted]. He can't see any of this. All he sees is a yellow truck and he says to himself this is a yellow truck transporting petrol for the BH army and I'm going target it would you agree with me that someone would think that way?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: They can think anything they like but let me also tell you that we were just 50 metres from where the fire was. So you can see whether it's a water truck, a cistern, or something else. We came there in broad daylight. The army wouldn't be transporting petrol in broad day like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I'm just asking you a hypothetical question that if somebody was on the right bank sees a yellow truck can, hypothetically speaking, think that they were transporting petrol. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I say this, then there's no confusion. At line 8, there's a reference to five or six metres. I'm quite sure that either wasn't what was said or what was meant. That's what appears in the English translation. Place yourself in the position of somebody five or six metres away.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes she said 500.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 500 to 600 metres is what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Praljak's question is a very interesting one. Now, in Mostar was it widely known that the fire trucks could be yellow, because mostly the fire engines are red? So did people know that there were yellow trucks that were being used as fire engines, as firefighters' trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just explain. Since we had the truck before the conflict that broke out with the HVO, we -- the fire brigade used that truck before the conflict, and everybody knew that this yellow truck was being used by the fire brigade, and it remained with the fire brigade, and everybody knew that it was a water truck supplying the population with water. So there was no doubt at all about its just being an ordinary truck carrying water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what you're saying is that before the conflict broke out the HVO knew full well that the fire brigade used this yellow truck or a yellow truck.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. The truck was used before the conflict by the fire brigade. The fire brigade had that truck before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Another question in this context. Would it be wise to drive towards a fire with a car full of petrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, of course not. Of course it wouldn't be reasonable, nor would you go out in full daylight with a truck like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understood it that the same people shot at the road while the fire was being extinguished, but that might not have been the same person.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, when we say that the HVO knew, which HVO? In Mostar, on both banks there were several thousand people, right? Along that length you agree there were many people?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So on the left bank and on the right bank were they all from Mostar? For example, on the left bank in the BH army, people from Gacko, Nevesinje, Stojnica [phoen], and so on, and on the right bank perhaps from Ljubuski, Siroki Brijeg, and so on. So did -- could these people have known that the yellow water truck transported water? Was that necessary -- did they necessarily know that when they went on duty?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, on our side, on our bank, everybody knew that that truck was the water truck, because during those three or four months everybody knew us very well and everybody saw the truck and knew it very well. Now, as to the right bank, well, people didn't have to know. Perhaps they'd never seen it. But the proximity itself --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's move on. We don't -- I don't have much time so I'm going to move on. Now, do you know why the truck wasn't brought to the place where the event took place for us to be able to see it on that location? You don't know why.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you don't know why Mr. Alija Jakupovic, for instance, who was hit, isn't testifying about the event? You don't know about that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I do know about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. You know about that. Right. Now, do you know that the BH army -- now, may we have a picture. May we have the 360-degree photograph played, please, so that we can establish some facts. And I'm going to ask you the following about that particular photograph. I'm going to ask you where the railway station is and you'll tell me, and I'm also going to ask you if you know whether part of the railway station was used or served as a warehouse for certain goods. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, and I'm quite certain that it didn't serve that purpose. It didn't serve any purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Are you quite sure of that in view of the documentation we have or what other witnesses have told us or aren't you sure? Stop there, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Since I passed by almost on a daily basis, I passed through the station and around the station almost every day, and I never saw a single soldier guarding anything or anybody move around there. It was an eerily empty space.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now the fact that you didn't see anyone, does that mean that you knew that there was nothing there? Or did you not see anything yourself?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask around. I didn't ask anybody. But the very fact that it was amend at this area, I can assume that there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me the following: Did the BH army at the material time control the entire area of Bijelo Polje, Vrapcici, or the left bank, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, what was the communication between that large area in Mostar if nobody ever passed by that way took that road? So what road and route did they take?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: The road by the railway station has nothing to do with that other communication line.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: The Bijelo Polje-Mostar road was taken at night. So it was the M-17 motorway or main road.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Were you a soldier? Did you go up on duty when you can claim with such certainty that it was only the main road that was used on at night? Do you know about that or are those your assumptions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, could you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The fact remains that the BH army controlled Vrapcici and Bijelo Polje and that there was communication.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: During the night.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In your view this was taking place during the night. You mentioned a location called Pasjak. Do you know that the 4th Corps of the BH army had its artillery?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: According to what you know, one segment of that artillery, was it in Pasjak, for example, mortars?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You're not aware of that. You have shown us and marked in this photo the right-hand side buildings as a possible location from which shots came against the vehicle. Is this known as Mostar 2 or Centar 2 in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the expert who dealt with your case expressly said that the shots came from Ledera are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: The Ledera and these buildings that are marked between Ledera and these buildings, the distance is some 50 metres. When I was marking the buildings, I said that I am not aware of the exact building, the entrance, the window from which the shots came. But if the distance between these buildings is 30 metres, then --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, these buildings that you showed are some several hundred metres long, and from Ledera to Centar 2 there are several hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: There's just one street, Crna Street, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please be so kind and tell us if you see the Ero Hotel, and if you see it, can you point the hotel for us? You should know that, next to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't have the image on my screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's wait for the image to appear on the witness's screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Could you please point to the Ero hotel. You see a tower and, next to that tower, as far as I know -- can this be placed on the ELMO. Mrs. Usher, we have a very good photo. Could this be placed on the ELMO. Hello. Could you please take the photo and put it on the ELMO. This will really be good because we will have a very good view of the area. Witness, can you see in the left-hand side corner a tower? Is that the Ero hotel?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you put number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Across the road from Ero you can see a balcony there. Would that be Ledera?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you put number 2 next to it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Could you please mark Centar 2 as you have marked before. Could you put a number 3 next to it or on it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, can you now see Witness that the 30-metre distance that you mentioned is far from being precise? We're trying to establish the truth here. Let's be precise talking about the things that we are familiar with. Now, to the right from the railway station, can you please put a number 4 on the railway station roof.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: This is the railway. Would -- to the right of it, would be the North Camp?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I can't see it in the photo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm not saying that you can see it, but I'm asking whether it is to the right of the railway station?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you put a number 5?
