utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So the BH army was in the North Camp as well? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: It had to communicate with the North Camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, tell me this. Let's assume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Please slow down. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the other Defence teams have donated you time, but there is another lawyer who has questions to put. Which Defence teams wish to put questions to the witness and for how long? Nobody? Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Probably about five minutes, Your Honour. Something like that. Depending on the answers as always, of course. So perhaps I could say if I reserve my 10-minute allocation then I should be safe, shouldn't I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: If this is for timing I will have one question at the moment for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Praljak, try to finish at 10 to 7.00, and if you finish quarter to 7.00 it will be even better.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's now propose another hypothesis. Let's imagine that out of the 35 or 40.000 people on the west bank, half of them are men. And let's say I was a criminal who wanted to kill people on the western bank. At how many places that you see in the photo could I in the morning, in the afternoon, between lunch and dinner, after lunch, place a sniper or an M-48 rifle on a balcony, at a window, at an entrance, put an optical device on that rifle and shoot at people whenever I decided to do so? Would that be a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: In a war, anything goes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: What would have been -- could that have been on the left bank of the Neretva? Was it possible for any of these embittered people for one reason or another, and there were a lot of reasons to be bitter, to take an M-45 rifle, to put an optical device in their pocket to hide in a certain place and remain hidden for two hours until they saw somebody on the left bank and shoot at them? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: It is possible but I doubt that this is the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: A doubt is one thing. A possibility is another. Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible. Well, if you ask me whether it is possible for this building to collapse, it is possible. It is certainly possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We have statements by the international representatives about people coming to the hospitals on the west bank who had been shot in that way and how many of them were Muslims. There is such information. There is no secret about that. So everything is possible. What would have been a possibility that, for example, if you were a commander there and that you were in command of a unit, for you to discover a noise of a bullet coming from a certain direction, how possible would it have been for you to discover who -- where the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Was there frequent shooting in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So it was true that there was frequent shooting?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And between the shots somebody is waiting at one of those places, hundreds of places that they could hide at and shoot at your lorry. Is that a realistic possibility?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: It is not a realistic possibility. It is a theory.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: It is a very realistic possibility, but this is where I'm going to stop and I'll move on to another subject. We have dealt with the problem of the North Camp and communication with the North Camp. It is true there was communication between the North Camp and -- but this communication had to pass by the railway station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, let's imagine that you were an HVO commander. Can we have the photo back. Can you see those hills over there? On those hills, was there HVO artillery or tanks?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I suppose that there were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You suppose there were. You were an HVO commander. You see a lorry or a water tank and you command the tank to blow that lorry up. How many shots does one tank have to fire in order to blow up the tank?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe two or three shots.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Two or three shots, you're saying. Do you know that the tank was also on mount Hum?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Hum is to the left of the photo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And this could have been done by a tank or a ZIS 68-millimetre or some other tool. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And the place where you were extinguishing the fire, was it also visible to the positions of the HVO artillery and their observers?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: The position was visible because there was a lot of smoke and this could be seen from all other the place. The lorry, however, was not visible but the building and the area were visible and were well marked by the smoke.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And let's say you are a commander of an operative zone or a HVO commander. Somebody reports to you there was a good target there. Could you have been blown that target up in -- under a minute?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I might have been able to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well, then. Could we have the 360-degree photograph shown once again, because we saw some hills over there and I would like to ask you some questions about them. And this would be the end of my cross-examination. Could you please put your initials on this photo and can we have an IC number for the photo, please. Yes, please, on this photo. Could you put your initials there, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 397.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now rotate the photo again? Can we start the rotation of the photo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did -- could you put your initials on the previous photo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back a little. Just a little, please. Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Look at the hill. It was also under the HVO control, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's move forward to the left. Let's move the photo. In the back behind the greenery is Hum, and, yes -- and there are also HVO units?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We are facing south; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's move on. Let's rotate a little further. Now we are going eastwards. The eastern side is approaching slowly. Stop. Now we can see some hills here.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Were these hills under the control of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: How far is the Republika Srpska army away from the -- from this place?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: From the hill or from the place where we are standing?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: From the hill.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: From the hill, it must have been some five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Five kilometres as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: No, not as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: To the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes, but when you look at this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: How much as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know I'm not an expert in that but it must have been two or three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: From there one could launch a mortar fire from the positions of the Republika Srpska army. I mean, one could do that. It is a possibility?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I don't know what range of the -- of that particular tool is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Five kilometres. And tell me, are you aware of the fact that throughout most of the conflict the Serbs were launching fire on both the left bank and the right bank as they willed? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: I know that they're shot from the right bank, but during that conflict there were very, very few and far between shots by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: There were shots from the right bank but there were also shots from the left bank, otherwise what would the artillery be for? But I'm asking you about this particular situation. If you know that there was fire, you should tell us there was fire or there wasn't fire. You shouldn't tell us there were very few and far between shots. What is that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: That means that during the war maybe a two-digit number of shells were fired from there, which means that there were under 20 -- under a hundred shells fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Recently we read a book written by one of your commanders and he said that in the month of September, we had a fanatical support by the artillery when we -- and -- shot at Croats. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I believe you, that you don't know. But if you don't know, you should say, "I don't know." I'm not putting words in your mouth but it is very difficult for one to say "I don't know" and then give us a number. Can we rotate the photo a little bit further. And now the last thing I would like to ask you. The Serbs are up there. Can you please put this on the ELMO and then that will be my last question to the witness. This is a very imprecise drawing of your lorry. Stop. Now look at these hilltops and, as you look at those hilltops, would you -- what would you say? Was this controlled by the BH army or by the Republika Srpska or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: This was the BiH army on the hilltops.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: On the hilltops?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Approximately thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Approximately then. Can you please look at my sketch, a very bad sketch of your lorry. And can you please draw the exact direction from which the bullet entered the driver's cabin.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: It entered somewhere somewhat in the middle of the driver's cabin below the roof. I believe that you can see it in the photo some 20 centimetres from the roof of the cabin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you put that, 20 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: This is where the driver was sitting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In what direction did the bullet come from?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: The bullet hit him to the back of the neck, so that would be the direction. At an angle. The shot wasn't straight. It was at an angle. Had it been from Ledera, the bullet would have hit the wall -- the door. However, since it was at an angle then it was Centar 2, the Centar 2 direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And if the shot had come from Ledera then the bullet, according to you, would have hit the door, would it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Then write Ledera for that other direction. And tell me this: The bullet that hit the man or, rather, grazed him, if it hit him he would have been dead, could you tell us how the bullet passed through his neck? Was it right to left or --

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Across his head like this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Parallel to the forehead?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, not parallel. This left side like this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So when he's facing the windscreen it is above the left ear; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience. Thank you, and would you sign or place your initials on that sketch, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 398.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know Mr. Petkovic has a couple of questions but I think our combined operations will finish at 6.55 Central European Time, with any luck.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness I just want to follow up that -- this question about the bullet going into the cabin of the truck. You described on the video how you -- where other shots you say hit the truck and you pointed out where this particular shot that we've just been looking at went in and it was just a little bit below the top of the cabin, behind and higher than you would have been sitting inside the truck. That seems to be a description of what you said on the video. You haven't said anything about where the bullet went out of the truck if it did. Do you have any knowledge yourself from your inspection of the truck as to whether and how the bullet went out of the cabin?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it didn't exit the truck. So when it hit the tin, it lodged there, or perhaps it went out of the window. Since it pierced part of the metal, it lost its strength and was either lodged in the second metal partition or maybe it went out the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's please just stick to what you saw and found yourself. You've described where it went in and you said you inspect the that back at the fire station. You said what it did next, which is -- "graze" is the word in the statement -- your colleague's head, and you're saying in your inspection you found no indication of where the bullet went out of the truck. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: First of all, we didn't look for the bullet at all, nor was it something that we would do. There were thousands of bullets like that, so is wasn't something that we did. The most important thing was that the man wasn't killed. As to the bullet, we didn't look further. Perhaps it was lodged in the cabin, but we didn't pay any attention to that. We didn't take time to find it or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're speeding up because the witness has answered my next question as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- you say in the statement that the bullet had entered the cabin from the back with an angle of about 45 degrees. Are you saying that there was something about the hole in the back of the cabin which told you that it had entered at that sort of angle?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, the hole itself on the truck and the imprint made by the bullet it as it entered, the imprint on the metal, you could establish that the bullet must have come at that kind of angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you either had sufficient previous experience of bullet holes, or if you didn't, it was absolutely obvious to you, was it, that it was at that sort of angle?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, you could see it. You could see that the bullet hadn't come in at right angles, straight. You can see the impact on the metal, and if you'd seen quite a few of those kinds of holes then you would have been able to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You see, the way you describe it, would you agree that the bullet seems to have gone in a straight line according to you, through the hole at that angle, carried on in a straight line, grazed your colleague's head? Do you agree that that's your description of what happened?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Yes. The bullet went straight. I didn't say the bullet didn't go straight, but in relation to the cabin, the bullet came in at an angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The reality is before you even looked at the truck back at the fire station you decided what had happened. You decided in your own mind where it had come from, and you didn't actually conduct any serious inspection at all because you didn't, for example, even look for the bullet. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: At that moment we were certain where the bullet came from and where the bullet would come from in a conflict and war of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions, but -- apparently Mr. Petkovic doesn't either, Your Honour. So the good news is we've finished.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have one?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead quickly then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked a hypothetical question. Could somebody shoot at their own men, the HVO shoot at their own soldiers? Do you know that the Mujahedins considered the Muslims who imbibed alcohol were worthless and they should be killed?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: We didn't know of any cases like that in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, just a moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I didn't say Mostar. I said, do you know that the Mujahedin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I'm going to ask you a question which has nothing to do with what Mr. Praljak was asking you. We know that the mortar fired while you were near -- while you were in hiding near the house. Now, you said [indiscernible] was there? I'm going to put a hypothetical to you. There was either another mortar shell that fell in the vicinity and that shrapnel dispersed and that one of these fragments, as you said, pierced the cabin of the truck at about 20 centimetres from the roof and grazed your colleague. What do you think about that hypothesis? Would that be quite unrealistic because you didn't hear any noise and you don't think that that could have been the result of a mortar being fired and falling and fragmenting?

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, that is not possible. It is not possible that the shrapnel -- that it was shrapnel, because the entry hole, well, you know -- you can tell what an entry hole looks like from a bullet and what a shrapnel looks like. And before that there were three shots, individual shots, several seconds apart, one after another until that final shot hit my colleague in the head. So there wasn't an explosion. You couldn't hear an explosion or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just wanted to test that hypothesis. Madam Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have one question, and I also need to remind myself to request an in-court number for the photograph that I showed the witness at the end of my examination-in-chief on which he marked a circle. So lest I not forget that after the question, I mention it now. Yes, quite. If the witness could be re-shown the photograph in order to initial it first, because I also -- and thank you for that reminder. I didn't remember that he hadn't signed it either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be then IC number 399.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Moving to my question as far as re-examination is concerned, it actually arises from Mr. Praljak's cross-examination at line 92.16. A question was asked by Mr. Praljak to which the witness was unable to respond, Your Honour having to intervene in order to slow proceedings somewhat, but it is nonetheless a question that merits an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I will repeat what you were asked by Mr. Praljak at line 92.16. What was said was: "Were you a soldier? Did you go up on duty when you can claim with such certainty that it was only the main road that was used, and at night? Do you know about that, or are those your assumptions?" Now, Witness, that is begging for an answer as to how you came to know with such certainty these events or indeed whether they were your assumptions.

utterances.speaker: ELVIR DEMIC
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: During the war I took that -- I never took that road, not once, and I wasn't a soldier, nor was I a member of any military organisation. Throughout the conflict, of course. The second point is this: The Mostar-Bijelo Polje road from Sutina to down here, Ina, was, as the crow flies, just 150 metres away from the HVO positions. So movement along that road was impossible during the day. Nothing could pass by that way during the day, only at night. At night, if you didn't have any lights or anything like that, you might be able to pass that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sir, that concludes your testimony. Thank you on behalf of my colleagues and myself for coming to The Hague to testify having been called by the Prosecution. We wish you every success in that noble occupation that you have. Tomorrow, Mr. Mundis, we have one witness. Don't give us his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, we have Witness A appearing tomorrow and continuing into Wednesday of this week, followed by the one remaining who is scheduled for Thursday. We have no further changes for this week's schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. I'd like to thank everybody, and we'll reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00, except for the witness, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
